tools.name: preview_pool
tools.description: Count people in overlap's peer-connection pool who are going through a similar personal situation. Use when the user asks whether another person shares their situation before deciding whether to join. Do not use for intersections of lists, sets or schedules, dating, or finding licensed professionals

tools.name: create_match_request
tools.description: Use this tool to save a private match request draft when the user wants to find a peer living through a similar personal situation. Write the match request from the current conversation. Write 2–5 sentences in the third person, and 200–1500 characters. Use the words of the user, not formal or clinic

tools.name: confirm_match_request
tools.description: Confirm one draft match request and add it to the matching pool. The other requests of the user do not change. It stays active until the user withdraws it. Call this ONLY after the user approves the exact stored text. Always pass its request_id.

tools.name: check_matches
tools.description: Where the user stands. It returns every current match request, the number of other people in the pool, and any match. Use it to answer what the user submitted, and who they matched with. A match can appear days later.

tools.name: get_match_details
tools.description: Get the full details of one match: what the other person wrote, why the two of them matched, something to open with, and where the match stands. It only reads. To accept, decline or block the match, call respond_to_match. Never promise an address.

tools.name: respond_to_match
tools.description: Record the one answer the user gave about a match: accept, decline or block. Call it only after the user has said which of the three they want. When both people accept, overlap opens a private conversation in the app. It also sends each person a link by email. Never promise an address. A decline cov

tools.name: withdraw_match_request
tools.description: Withdraw one match request, either a draft or an open one. Always pass its request_id. If it is unclear which one the user means, call check_matches first. The other requests of the user stay active. This voids a pending match from this request. It keeps a match that both people accepted.

findings.title: Anomalously long tool description
findings.detail: Description of "create_match_request" is 1581 chars, far longer than this server's median (289). Overlong descriptions are a common place to bury instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: create_match_request · Private data: create_match_request, respond_to_match · Public sink: create_match_request, respond_to_match.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: create_match_request · Private data: create_match_request, respond_to_match · Public sink: create_match_request, respond_to_match

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
